title: Photosynthesis
content: Photosynthesis is the process in which plants, algae, and some bacteria use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into sugars, releasing oxygen. In plants it mainly occurs in chloroplasts. The light reactions happen in the thylakoid membranes, producing ATP and NADPH, while the Calvin cycle in the stroma uses these to fix carbon dioxide into glucose.

title: Seasons
content: Earth's seasons are caused by its roughly 23.5-degree axial tilt. As Earth orbits the Sun, each hemisphere alternately receives more direct sunlight and longer days; distance from the Sun is not the main cause. The solstices mark the longest and shortest days, while equinoxes have roughly equal day and night.

title: Newton's laws
content: Newton's laws connect force and motion: objects retain velocity unless a net force acts (inertia), acceleration equals net force divided by mass (F=ma), and forces occur in equal-and-opposite pairs (action-reaction). These laws form the foundation of classical mechanics and apply to most everyday-scale phenomena.

title: Fractions
content: A fraction represents parts of a whole: the denominator gives the number of equal parts and the numerator gives how many are selected. Equivalent fractions name the same quantity at different scales. Operations include finding common denominators for addition, cross-multiplying for comparison, and inverting for division.

title: Supply and demand
content: In a competitive market, demand describes how much buyers want at each price while supply describes how much sellers offer. Price tends toward a point where quantities supplied and demanded balance (equilibrium), though real markets have constraints like monopolies, externalities, and information asymmetry.

title: Machine learning
content: Machine learning builds models that learn patterns from examples. Training adjusts model parameters; validation guides choices; and testing estimates performance on unseen data. Key paradigms include supervised learning (labeled data), unsupervised learning (pattern discovery), and reinforcement learning (reward-based). Generalization matters more than memorizing training samples.

title: The water cycle
content: Solar energy drives evaporation and plant transpiration. Water vapor condenses into clouds, falls as precipitation, and returns through runoff or groundwater, continually moving among ocean, land, and atmosphere. Human activities like deforestation and urbanization can significantly alter local water cycles.

title: DNA
content: DNA stores hereditary information in sequences of four nucleotide bases (adenine, thymine, guanine, cytosine). Cells copy DNA before division through replication, and genes can be transcribed into RNA that helps direct protein production through translation. Mutations in DNA can lead to genetic variation.

title: Gravity
content: Gravity is a fundamental force that attracts objects with mass toward each other. Newton described it as proportional to the product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of distance. Einstein's general relativity reframes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

title: The solar system
content: Our solar system consists of the Sun, eight planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, and comets. The inner rocky planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) differ from the outer gas and ice giants (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune). The asteroid belt separates these two groups, and the Kuiper Belt lies beyond Neptune.

title: Evolution
content: Evolution is the change in heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations. Natural selection, proposed by Darwin and Wallace, acts on genetic variation: organisms better adapted to their environment tend to survive and reproduce more. Genetic drift, mutation, and gene flow also drive evolution.

title: Electricity
content: Electricity involves the flow of electric charge, typically electrons, through a conductor. Voltage (potential difference) drives current through resistance, described by Ohm's law (V=IR). Circuits can be series (single path) or parallel (multiple paths). Electrical power equals voltage times current (P=VI).
